bible_refs.method: allusion: παραλύσει … ὁ ἀποκτείνας αὐτόν restates the LXX verse quoted in ep-open
bible_refs.note: The author paraphrases the verse while explaining it.

bible_refs.method: wording: 'ποσάκις ἁμαρτήσει εἰς ἐμὲ ὁ ἀδελφός μου καὶ ἀφήσω αὐτῷ; ἕως ἑπτάκις;'
bible_refs.note: Peter's question, quoted without the opening 'Lord'.

bible_refs.method: wording: 'οὐ λέγω σοι ἕως ἑπτάκις ἀλλὰ ἕως ἑβδομηκοντάκις ἑπτά'
bible_refs.note: Rendered 'seventy times seven' because the letter's argument is that the Lord multiplied seven rather than changing the number.

choices.why: Perfect passive of τάσσω: a standing decree of divine judgment.

choices.term: πῶς ἐν τῷ ἑπτάκις πληροῦται καὶ τὰ ἐκδικούμενα
choices.english: how are the punishments fulfilled in the “seven times”
choices.why: One question; τὰ ἐκδικούμενα is the subject of πληροῦται.
rejected: how is justice fulfilled, and what are the things avenged (adds a question)

choices.why: πέφυκε with infinitive: to be disposed by nature.
The argument is that the Lord multiplied seven rather than changing the number.

pass_a_gloss: [continuing 'Since…'] it has been appointed for Cain to pay in full seven times the penalty of the sins, he will release, it says, this thing decreed upon him by the divine judgment — the one who killed him. This is the sense occurring from here on the first reading. But since the mind of the more industrious is by nature to search the depths, it seeks the just: how in the seven times is it fulfilled, and the things avenged? Whether the things sinned are seven, one the sin, but seven upon the one the punishments? Always then Scripture limits the number of the forgiveness of sins in the seven. 'How many times,' he says, 'will my brother sin against me, and I will forgive him?' (it is Peter saying to the Lord) 'Up to seven times?' Then the answer of the Lord: 'I do not say to you up to seven times, but up to seventy times seven.' For not to another number did the Lord pass over, but the [seven…].
pass_b_english: …it has been ordained that Cain should pay the penalty for his sins seven times over, the one who kills him, it says, will release him from what divine judgment decreed against him (Genesis 4:15). This is the sense that presents itself here on a first reading.

But since the mind of the more diligent naturally searches the depths, it looks for the justice of it: how are the punishments fulfilled in the “seven times”? Are the sins seven? Or is the sin one, and the punishments for that one sin seven?

Now Scripture always limits the number for the forgiveness of sins to seven. “How often,” he says, “will my brother sin against me, and I forgive him?” (it is Peter speaking to the Lord) “Up to seven times?” (Matthew 18:21). Then comes the Lord’s answer: “I do not say to you up to seven times, but up to seventy times seven” (Matthew 18:22). For the Lord did not move on to another number, but…
source_text:
τέτακται ἑπτάκις ἀποπληρῶσαι τὴν δίκην τῶν ἡμαρτημένων τὸν Καΐν, παραλύσει
, φησὶν, τούτῳ τῷ ὑπὸ τῆς θείας κρίσεως ἐπ' αὐτῷ δεδογμένον, ὁ ἀποκτείνας αὐτόν.
Οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ νοῦς ὁ ἐντεῦθεν ἀπὸ τῆς πρώτης ἀναγνώσεως ὑποπίπτων.
Ἐπειδὴ δὲ ἐρευνᾷν πέφυκε τὰ βάθη τῶν φιλοπονωτέρων ἡ διάνοια, ἐπιζητεῖ
τὸ δίκαιον, πῶς ἐν τῷ ἑπτάκις πληροῦται καὶ τὰ ἐκδικούμενα; πότερον τὰ
ἁμαρτηθέντα ἑπτά ἐστιν, ἓν μὲν τὸ ἁμάρτημα, ἑπτὰ δὲ ἐπὶ τῷ ἑνὶ αἱ κολάσεις; Ἀεὶ μὲν
οὖν ἡ Γραφὴ τὸν τῆς ἀφέσεως τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν ἀριθμὸν ἐν τοῖς ἑπτὰ περιορίζει.
Ποσάκις, φησὶ, ἁμαρτήσει εἰς ἐμὲ ὁ ἀδελφός μου, καὶ ἀφήσω αὐτῷ (ὁ Πέτρος ἐστὶ
λέγων τῷ Κυρίῳ); ἕως ἑπτάκις; Εἶτα ἀπόκρισις τοῦ Κυρίου· Οὐ λέγω σοι ἕως ἑπτάκις,
ἀλλ' ἕως ἑβδομηκοντάκις ἑπτά· οὐ γὰρ ἐπ' ἄλλον ἀριθμὸν μετέβη ὁ Κύριος, ἀλλὰ τὸν
reviewer: claude (Wave A review, clause by clause against the Greek)
review_notes: Author: this letter is Basil of Caesarea's Letter 260, to Bishop Optimus. PG 77 prints it among the letters of Cyril of Alexandria as Letter 80. Identity checked against the Greek and against the NPNF Series 2 vol. 8 English of Basil's Letter 260 (used only to confirm identity, not for wording).
Reviewer rv0 fixes applied before merge: one question, not two, for πῶς … πληροῦται καὶ τὰ ἐκδικούμενα; 'naturally searches' for πέφυκε (no 'drawn').
Checked clean: Matthew 18:21-22 wording; the supplied 'Or' after πότερον (no ἤ in the copy-text).
Copy-text oddities rendered by sense: dative τούτῳ τῷ for an expected accusative; no ἤ after πότερον.
